title: Governments from 33 countries are considering a $9 billion replenishment for the International Development Association (IDA), aimed at supporting development projects in the poorest nations over the next three years. The IDA, a key source of concessional lending, has previously extended $30 billion in credits to 79 countries, focusing heavily on agriculture and rural development. Additionally, the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) is proposing an $8.4 billion capital increase to enhance its lending capacity. A recent $21.5 million loan to Cameroon will support rural development, benefiting 85,000 families and improving agricultural productivity. Furthermore, a railway re-alignment project in Cameroon aims to reduce derailments and increase transport capacity, funded by various international partners.
